Integrate three finished branches of the JusPrin project chat's skills work into one branch for Kenneth to merge. Start from local `jusprin-newui` at 4ec21799ce (unpushed; do not push). Create branch `claude/skills-integrated`. Report, untracked at your worktree root as `skills-integration-report.md`, four parts (problem, what changed, tests and results, remaining issues), plain English for someone who did not see this. Never commit the report. Commit on your branch with plain messages and no attribution lines; do not merge into `jusprin-newui`, Kenneth does that.

## What you are merging

Each is one commit on 4ec21799ce, with its report untracked at the root of its worktree. Read all three reports first.

1. `claude/skill-slice-failed` (c7ed56d027; report `.claude/worktrees/cool-bardeen-7f40f5/skill-slice-failed-report.md`): per-plate `slice_failure` in the workspace snapshot, recorded by the adapter from a hook in `Plater::reslice` and worded by the print-issue monitor; `slice_start` decides at once between a run that began, nothing needed, and a refusal; `wait` and `finished` removed; the app starts a turn when the model's slice ends after its turn; the `slice-failed` skill; a shell-harness race fix; Kenneth's beginner rule added to the standing prompt's Replies section.
2. `claude/skill-print-issues` (2381d07aaa; report `.claude/worktrees/angry-rhodes-dd8e89/skill-print-issues-report.md`): per-plate `slice_warnings` summary from the monitor; the `print-issues` skill fired on a print-issue chip's request and on new warnings after a slice; the print-issue bullet removed from the prompt.
3. `claude/skill-setup-changed` (77d9d3dbdf; report `.claude/worktrees/quizzical-jepsen-f3a53c/skill-setup-changed-report.md`): `intent_update`'s reply states the purpose change and the setup in force; the workspace block gains `setupUncheckedChange` and plan validity; the `project-setup-changed` skill, which gives way to `file-loaded`; the Preparing section reduced to one bullet; two rules moved into tool descriptions.

Merge in that order. `git merge-tree` shows every pair conflicts: 1 with 2 in 24 files (the shared per-plate record in `Workspace.hpp`, the plate JSON in `AgentHost::context_json`, `OpenAIResponsesAgent::workspace_json` and `slicing_section_result`, the `slicing_plate` schema, `PrintIssue.hpp/.cpp`, the adapter and `ShellController` wiring, `SkillTrigger`, `workspace_inspect`'s description, `skills.test.ts`, the recorder and the eval files); 1 with 3 in 11 and 2 with 3 in 10, mostly `AgentHost`, `AgentProtocol.hpp`, `skills.test.ts`, the tool guide and the eval files. Resolve by keeping both sides' behaviour; where the two sides wrote the same sentence twice in different words (the `workspace_inspect` description), write it once: branch 2's report suggests "whether each plate's slice is current, what it warned about and why its last slice did not succeed".

## Decisions Kenneth has made for this integration

- **One finding record, not two.** Branches 1 and 2 each added a per-plate record with the same fields (severity, OrcaSlicer's message, setting, code, object, sequence): `SliceFailure` and `SliceWarnings`. Make them one shape: a plate's findings from its last slice attempt, with a kind (refused, failed, warning), the count and how many the person ignored, and the first one to read, critical first. Keep each branch's firing rule and told-list semantics (the `slice-failed` skill fires once per failure, the `print-issues` skill once per set of new warnings); unify the bookkeeping only where the two sides are duplicates (`m_slice_failures_told` beside `m_slice_warnings_told`, `fire_on_new_slice_failure` beside `fire_print_issues`). The model's view in the workspace block and tool replies stays short.
- **The bed-temperature warning is told to the model.** Branch 2 left code `1000C001` out of the summary to match `slice_report`; Kenneth wants the summary to match what the chip shows the person, so include it (and the duplicate timelapse code `1000C003` only if the chip shows it). Say in the report whether `slice_report` should follow, and leave it as is.
- **The standing prompt.** Write the one fixture the three branches imply: Role unchanged; When to act with three bullets, the print bullet as branch 3 wrote it, the print-issue bullet gone, the repeated-request bullet gone; Grounding unchanged; no Preparing section, with the last procedural sentence ("Before calling a print ready, slice its plate and check slice_report (slice_inspect when needed) against their requirements; fix or explain what remains.") folded into the print bullet as one clause, since the warnings now reach the model without a call and "their requirements" has lost its referent, for example "A print request: a setup that suits the print's purpose, recorded with intent_update, checked, and verified by a slice whose findings you have read before you call it ready."; Replies with Kenneth's beginner rule from branch 1. Report the byte count; expect about 1,900 bytes. Update `projectInstructions.ts`, its fixture and `projectInstructions.test.ts` together.
- **Do not change the Slice button.** A person still cannot press Slice on a plate OrcaSlicer refused; leave that alone.
- No sentence anywhere may say "approve", "authorize", "confirm before" or "ask the user then call again"; tool-call approval was removed on 2026-10-07.

## After the merge

- Regenerate `tests/project_prompt/project_tools.json` from the registry.
- Re-record `tests/project_prompt/requests.json` once with the shell harness's `--project-prompt-requests`; the recorder's skill checks (`prompt_is_any_skill` and the per-point `"skill": "<name>"` checks) must know all four skills; the union of the three branches' cases must render (`run_prompt_tests.py --render-only`), and `test_steps.py` must pass with every branch's offline tests kept.
- Build and run everything on the merged tree, Release if disk is short: `agent_bridge_tests`, `jusprin_tests`, `workspace_contract_tests`, the real-adapter workspace harness, the shell harness default scenario plus `--print-issues` and `--external-project-history`, AgentUI vitest and `tsc` after `jusprin_web` is rebuilt, `test_steps.py`, the recorder. Every test the three branches added must still pass; report counts. cmake is at `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake`; nohup long builds and watch the log; `cd` into your worktree in every Bash call.
- Update `agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md` once for all three (each branch edited it).
- Report line counts added and removed against 4ec21799ce, excluding `requests.json`, and the prompt, skills and descriptions byte counts.

## Measurement

Do not run a live model batch; Kenneth runs live evals himself. Propose in the report the paired run: every case once, the prompt at 4ec21799ce rendered with `--prompt-rev` against the integrated prompt from the checkout, same day, DeepSeek V4 Flash on the pinned hosts with the pinned judge; estimate requests and tokens from the README's last batches. Note which cases have no "before" (the ones whose point did not exist or whose request now carries a skill).

=================== .claude/worktrees/cool-bardeen-7f40f5/skill-slice-failed-report.md
# Slice-failed skill, the failure fact, and asynchronous slicing

Branch `claude/skill-slice-failed`, one commit (c7ed56d027, the six commits below squashed on 2026-10-18) on 4ec21799ce, the commit on local `jusprin-newui` that renamed the model-arrived skill to file-loaded. The branch was first built on 1435f4c817 and moved with `git rebase --onto`; 1435f4c817 is no longer in its history. None is pushed or merged. Tip: c7ed56d027. The hashes below name the commits before the squash; the old tip 460cc6a0bf has the same tree.

- 551c25787f records the failure, makes `slice_start` decide inside the call, and adds the skill.
- 4431f41e86 removes `wait` and `finished`, and has the app start a chat turn when a slice the model started ends after its turn (section 2b).
- 7e793d8cea fixes a race in the shell harness that predates this branch (see the shell harness note in section 3).
- 2fe9e8290d finishes the rename in what this branch added, and records `requests.json` again on the new base.
- bbe43f2fc9 adds Kenneth's beginner rule to the standing prompt (2,364 to 2,522 bytes), rewords the skills and the refusal judge to match, and records `requests.json` again; it was written in another session and committed here (section 3c).

## 1. Problem

When the model asked JusPrin to slice and OrcaSlicer refused the plate (for example Bambu PETG HF on the Cool Plate), the model was told the slice had started. `slice_start` posts the same event as the Slice button and, without `wait`, returned `started: true` straight away. OrcaSlicer then ran its own check, refused, showed a notification and sliced nothing; none of that reached the reply. With `wait: true` the call polled the app's tick for "seen running, then stopped". A refusal never starts a run, so the call sat for 15 minutes and returned `finished: false` with no reason. `slice_report` for the unsliced plate gave only `valid: false`. These are the "slice reports success with nothing sliced" and "hangs on retry" faults seen live on 2026-10-15.

The reason was not lost in the app. The print-issue monitor already reads OrcaSlicer's message, the setting key and the object for the active plate. It just never reached the model.

A second finding came up while testing. A person cannot press Slice on a plate OrcaSlicer's check has already refused. JusPrin's status-row button and OrcaSlicer's own Slice controls (including the Ctrl+R shortcut) are both off for such a plate. The check runs about half a second after each edit. So the person's way into a refusal is Slice all, which slices plate by plate and is refused at the first plate it cannot slice.

## 2. What changed

**The fact, recorded once.** Each plate in the workspace snapshot now has `slice_failure`, next to `sliced` and `invalidated_by`. It holds:

- whether OrcaSlicer refused the plate or the run failed partway (`refused` or `failed`);
- the severity, as the issue list rates it;
- OrcaSlicer's message, unchanged;
- the setting key and the object, when OrcaSlicer names them;
- the native check code;
- a sequence number.

The workspace adapter (`OrcaWorkspaceAdapter`) records it at two moments:

- **OrcaSlicer declines to start.** I added a three-line hook to `Plater.cpp` (`report_slice_declined()`, declared in the new `Workspace/SliceRequests.hpp`). It fires where `Plater::reslice` finds the plate invalid, where it skips a plate whose last run failed with nothing changed since, and where a slice-all reaches a plate it cannot slice.
- **A run fails partway.** OrcaSlicer's completion event carries the error. The record is made at the slice-status change that follows, once OrcaSlicer has finished with the plate.

The record is cleared when the plate slices, and hidden from the moment a new run on that plate starts. Recording the same reason again keeps the same sequence number, so pressing Slice twice is one failure, not two. Every adapter registers its own listener, so a second adapter (the workspace harness creates several) never silences the shell's.

**Why the adapter records it and the monitor words it.** The monitor (`PrintIssueMonitor`) is the only place that already turns OrcaSlicer's notice into message, setting and object; it reruns OrcaSlicer's `validate` for the parts the notice leaves out. But it cannot be the store, for three reasons:

- it reports only the active plate, and forgets a plate's validation when you look at another plate;
- it does not know when a slice was asked for, so it cannot tell a refusal from an edit that fails validation;
- the shell creates it, and the workspace harness has none.

So the adapter keeps the per-plate record and knows the moment. At that moment it calls a reader function, which the shell wires to `PrintIssueMonitor::slice_failure()`. That function refreshes the monitor and returns its first blocker, via the new `slice_failure_of()` in `PrintIssue.cpp`. The message is never worked out a second time. Without a reader the record says only "OrcaSlicer did not start slicing this plate."

**Everywhere the model reads.** All of these are built from the snapshot, so the reason reaches the model whether the model or the person asked for the slice:

- the `<workspace>` block on every message;
- the slicing section of tool replies;
- the workspace context in every tool reply;
- `slice_report` of an unsliced plate (the full record, plus the check code and object name).

The model's view is short: kind, severity, message, setting, objectId.

**`slice_start` decides inside the call.** After posting the event, the coordinator reads the snapshot and reports one of three outcomes:

- a run began (`started: true`);
- the plates were already sliced and unchanged (`started: false, alreadySliced: true`);
- OrcaSlicer refused (`started: false` with `reason`, in a succeeded call).

(The first commit kept `wait`, finished from the workspace change. The second commit removes it; see 2b.)

Two related fixes:

- The adapter refused any plate already marked invalid with its own generic "cannot be sliced as it stands", before OrcaSlicer was asked. It now passes such a plate through to OrcaSlicer, which refuses it in its own words. A plate that does not fit the printer is recorded as refused in the words of OrcaSlicer's notice.
- The slicing section's `handle` used to name a run from a previous project, because action ids restart with each project. It is now cleared when the project changes.

The tool description now says what happens when OrcaSlicer refuses. `project_tools.json` is regenerated.

**The skill.** `AgentUI/src/skills/slice-failed/SKILL.md` has trigger `slice_failed` (a new `Protocol::SkillTrigger::kSliceFailed`) and is 3,601 bytes, against 6,982 for the file-loaded skill. It covers:

- refused versus failed;
- that OrcaSlicer's check alone has about 150 messages, and the model should not assume it knows them;
- how to read a message (the setting key via `settings_search` or `settings_get`; the object narrows where);
- that the check stops at the first problem it finds;
- that a problem is fixed only when a new slice no longer reports it;
- that the filament and plate pairing is the person's decision, while toolpath settings are the model's;
- a seven-row guide to the message families in `Print::validate`.

The host fires it on the first request that carries a failure the model has not read about. That is the result of the model's own `slice_start`, the turn the app starts when the model's slice fails after its turn, or the next request after the person's slice. It fires once per failure, and nothing stores it. The host stays generic: `fire_skill` takes any trigger.

**Standing prompt: unchanged.** No sentence of `projectInstructions.fixture.txt` is fully carried by the fact or the skill. The nearest one, "Before calling a print ready, slice its plate and check slice_report", is about readiness in general, not refusals.

**Size of the first commit.** Excluding `requests.json`:

| Area | Lines added | Lines removed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source and docs | 530 | 83 |
| Tests and eval | 740 | 40 |

## 2b. The second commit: slicing is asynchronous everywhere

You decided, through another session, to remove `wait` and to have the app speak when the model's slice ends. The reasoning: a slice runs in the background, and the model has to handle "started, outcome not known yet" anyway, because a waited call could also end without an outcome (the deadline, a missed event). One path is simpler than two.

**Part 1: `wait` and `finished` removed.** `slice_start` loses its `wait` argument, and no reply carries `finished`. Gone from the coordinator:

- the `SliceWait` map and `finish_slice_waits`;
- the 15-minute deadline, the test clock (`set_clock_for_testing`), and the tick's overdue check;
- the tick's skip for waiting calls;
- the wait-finishing part of the workspace subscription.

The three outcomes decided inside the call stay. A run that began now says in its reply: "The slice has started; its result is not known yet. While your turn goes on, the workspace in each tool result shows it; when it ends after your turn, the app tells you." The description says the same.

Deleted tests:

- "a slice started with wait returns when the run ends…";
- "a waiting slice_start finishes when the workspace reports the run's end, or at its deadline";
- the `wait` iterations and `finished` checks in the three-outcome test;
- the `validate_call` check of `wait`.

No test checks that `wait` is gone.

**Part 2: the app starts a turn when the model's slice ends after its turn.** The coordinator already saw the run end in its workspace subscription. It now hands the end to the host through `set_slice_ended`, the way `set_agent_project_opened` hands over a project open. The host acts on it at the next timer tick, not inside OrcaSlicer's event. It posts an app note and calls `start_turn`, which queues the turn if another is running. The note says "The slice of Plate 1 finished." or "OrcaSlicer stopped the slice of Plate 1: <OrcaSlicer's words>".

The design choices you asked to see stated:

- **(a) The turn's input.** It is the note's text with a prefix: "JusPrin app note, not the person's words: …". I added no field. The outcome as data is already in that request's `<workspace>` block (`sliced`, the estimate, `sliceFailure`), built from the snapshot as on every request.
- **(b) History.** The note is not replayed in later requests. Project-chat notes stay out of context (`notes_in_context` is off), because the workspace block carries the state; the model's own reply to the note stays in history. None of the file-report machinery is used.
- **(c) Which conversation.** The one whose turn called `slice_start`, found through the call's correlation id, even if the person has switched chats since.
- **(d) Rendering.** An ordinary note in the existing note rendering, with no new message kind.
- **(e) Trigger.** One callback from the existing subscription, at the point where the run's "in flight" flag is cleared. No polling.
- **(f) Once.** The callback fires once per run, because clearing that flag is what fires it. On a failure the slice-failed skill rides on this same turn, through the existing once-per-failure rule. It is not a second message.

When nothing is posted:

- the turn that called `slice_start` is still going (its next tool result shows the outcome);
- the person or an MCP client started the slice;
- the run neither sliced nor failed, as when it is stopped through `activity_cancel` or the Cancel button;
- the project changed in the meantime.

**Two redundant guards removed while proving the tests.** I first added a guard to `activity_cancel` and a second project check in the host. Breaking either one left every test passing, because another rule already covered each case: a stopped run is neither sliced nor failed, and the project change already clears the run's handle. Both are gone, as are the `m_slice_running` resets the first commit had added for the same cases.

**Size of the second commit.** Excluding `requests.json`:

| Part | Lines added | Lines removed |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Part 1: remove `wait` and `finished` (code, tests, tool list, eval script, docs) | 50 | 205 |
| Part 2: the slice-ended turn | 256 | 1 |

Part 2's added lines break down as:

- 70 lines in the host and coordinator;
- 170 lines of tests;
- 11 lines in the recorder;
- 5 lines of docs and eval runner.

In the coordinator alone, Part 1 removed 72 lines and added 9; Part 2 added a 6-line callback.

## 3. Tests and results

All suites were run on this branch (Release build).

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `agent_bridge_tests` | 316 cases, all pass |
| `jusprin_tests` | 111 cases, all pass |
| `workspace_contract_tests` | 42 cases, all pass |
| AgentUI vitest | 424 tests, all pass; `tsc` clean |
| `python3 tests/project_prompt/test_steps.py` | 17 tests, OK |
| `run_prompt_tests.py --render-only` | 22 cases, 66 requests at 3 runs |
| Real-adapter workspace harness | PASS (see below) |
| Shell harness default scenario | PASS, 4 of 4 runs after 7e793d8cea (see note) |
| Recorder (`--project-prompt-requests`) | PASS, 22 points |

The table is for the second commit. The first commit's runs gave the same results, with 314 agent-bridge cases.

**The second commit's tests fail without its code.** I broke each rule on its own, rebuilt, and checked:

| Rule broken | Tests failing |
| --- | --- |
| The coordinator never reports the end | 3 test cases |
| The host posts during the same turn | 1 |
| The end is reported twice | 2 |
| A stopped run is reported | the cancel case |
| The old project's handle is kept | the project-change case |

The new tests cover:

- one app turn after a successful run, and one after a failure, carrying the slice-failed skill;
- once per run;
- nothing while the calling turn goes on;
- a turn queued behind another turn and started after it;
- nothing for the person's slice, a cancelled run, or a replaced project.

**The new unit tests fail without the change.** I broke each part on purpose (the change no longer finishing the wait, no synchronous decision, no deadline, the host never firing the skill, no failure in the workspace block or `slice_report`) and rebuilt. Every new test case failed, and so did the existing wait test. The stale-handle check also fails with its fix removed. The new tests cover:

- the three start outcomes;
- `slice_report` carrying the reason;
- the reason kept through a repeated refusal and cleared once a run starts;
- the skill on the refused `slice_start` result and not on the next request;
- the skill on the person's next request, once per failure, again for a new mid-run failure, and not after a success;
- the short form in the `<workspace>` block;
- `slice_failure_of`'s order of preference.

**Shell harness note.** Before the harness fix, the default scenario failed in 4 of 6 runs on this branch, and passed 2 of 2 on the base commit. Each failure was a timeout at one of two steps, `second_conversation_reply_completes` or `tool_run_succeeded`.

I added temporary diagnostics to a failing run. At the stuck step the host was idle (no stream, no running tool, no slice), and the new chat held no message at all. So the scripted message never reached the host.

The cause is a race in the harness, and it predates this branch:

- The page's send carries the chat its own state holds as active.
- The host refuses a message for any other chat as `stale_conversation` (since 2026-10-05).
- The harness sent right after creating a chat, or right after reloading the page, sometimes before the page's state had caught up.

7e793d8cea makes those two sends wait, inside the page, until the page shows the host's active chat. After that, 4 of 4 runs passed.

Two caveats:

- Those four runs ran at a low load average (about 5), while most of the earlier failures were at 30 to 65, so the runs alone are weak evidence. The refusal path itself I read in the code.
- I can't say why the branch lost the race more often than the base did. Two base runs are too few to show a real difference.

Two existing tests started a slice on a plate already marked sliced, which OrcaSlicer would not run. They now invalidate the slice first, as an edit would.

**Real OrcaSlicer.** The real-adapter harness gained 17 checks. It sets Bambu PETG HF on the Cool Plate and slices for real through the shell's own adapter, with the monitor as reader:

- nothing runs;
- the reason is on the plate before the call returns, as kind `refused`, code `filament_not_match_bed_type`, in OrcaSlicer's words;
- the revision advances;
- OrcaSlicer's own `reslice` again keeps the same failure and revision;
- on the Textured PEI Plate a run starts, the reason disappears, and the plate slices.

The real message is "Plate 1: Cool Plate is not suggested for use printing filament 1 (Bambu PETG HF). If you still want to do this print job, please set this filament's bed temperature to a number that is not zero." OrcaSlicer rewrites the raw "does not support filament" string from `Print::validate` into this before showing it. The skill quotes the rewritten form.

**Recorder.** The recorder now accepts a skill name on a point (`"skill": "slice-failed"`), checks that point ends with exactly that skill, and checks that no other point and not the next request carries it. It also accepts a person's Slice or Slice-all press as a step, and `{{workspace/plateId/N}}`. The two new points:

- `slice-refused-by-tool`: the request carrying the refused `slice_start` result.
- `slice-refused-then-ready`: two plates, the second on the Cool Plate; the person presses Slice all (plate 1 slices, plate 2 is refused) and asks "is it ready to print?".

The other 20 points changed only in timestamps, temporary paths and ids, except `after-slice` in the second commit:

- Its `slice_start` result now shows the run in flight, with the "not known yet" sentence. Before, that point came after the run had ended.
- Its recorded reads were taken after the run ended. The recorder takes 113 reads at that point, and the slice finished meanwhile. So a `slice_report` there is answered with the finished slice, as a read a few seconds later would be.
- The case still passes on `slice_report`, or on a reply that does not claim readiness. Its docstring says the above.

When a model-started slice ends after a recorded turn, the app now starts a turn in that conversation. The recorder answers such a turn with nothing before setting up the next conversation, so it cannot leak into the next one. No point records it.

## 3b. Live batch (run 2026-10-17, 3 runs per case)

Run on the recording from 4431f41e86, before the rebase onto 4ec21799ce: DeepSeek V4 Flash on the pinned hosts, with the pinned OpenAI judge. 3 of 9 runs passed.

| Case | Passed | Failed | Unobserved |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `slice-refused-by-tool` | 1 | 2 | 0 |
| `slice-refused-then-ready` | 1 | 2 | 0 |
| `after-slice` | 1 | 0 | 2 |

Usage: 18 model requests, 298,443 input tokens (193,024 cached) and 3,621 output; 10 judge requests, 22,035 input and 3,064 output.

**The refusal cases.** All four failures are the judge's "reason left out or invented", and in every one the judge says the reply did explain the refusal. It failed them for extra explanation:

- the Cool Plate being meant for PLA, and PETG possibly damaging its coating (two runs);
- "the filament preset has no bed temperature for this plate type" (two runs). That is the skill's own table wording, and OrcaSlicer's message itself says to set the bed temperature to a non-zero number.

No run claimed the print was ready, sliced again unchanged, or changed the setup without asking. The passes were a `printer_setup_preview` of the Textured PEI Plate (a read), and a reply that quoted OrcaSlicer's words.

My reading: the case's judge question ("without giving any other cause") is stricter than the skill. It counts the skill's own explanation as an invented cause. Rewording it to fail only on a cause that contradicts or goes beyond OrcaSlicer's message and the skill's table would make these counts mean what the case intends. I haven't changed it, because the question is yours to set.

**`after-slice`.** One run read `slice_report` and passed. In the other two the model said "Still slicing (80% done) — let me check again" and called `workspace_inspect` until the runner's limit of 3 reads. The recorded `workspace_inspect` answer was taken while the run was at 80%, and the runner replays it unchanged, so polling could never see the end. In the app the same polling would see the run finish, at the cost of one full request per poll, roughly 12,000 to 20,000 input tokens each here.

This is the cost `wait` used to avoid. With `wait`, this case passed 3 of 3 in the 2026-10-17 baseline. Now that the slice-ended turn exists, telling the model to end its turn rather than poll would be a wording change in the tool result's note or the description; that is your call.

## 3c. Before and after the beginner rule (run 2026-10-18)

bbe43f2fc9 adds the beginner rule to the standing prompt, rewords the slice-failed skill's "cause" sentence, and loosens the refusal judge. These are the two refusal cases, 3 runs each, on the same day, on DeepSeek V4 Flash on the pinned hosts with the pinned judge. "Before" is the prompt at 2fe9e8290d (`--prompt-rev`); "after" is bbe43f2fc9. Only the standing prompt differs between the two: the skill text is in `requests.json` and the judge question is in the runner, so both batches used the new versions of those.

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `slice-refused-by-tool` | 2 of 3 | 2 of 3 |
| `slice-refused-then-ready` | 3 of 3 | 3 of 3 |

- **The one failure on each side is the same.** In `slice-refused-by-tool` run 2, the reply explained the plate and filament mismatch and what to do, but never said the plate was not sliced. The judge requires that.

A `cmake --build` started with the Bash tool's `run_in_background` is still
bound by that call's `timeout` (default 120 s, max 600 s). When it fires the
build log ends with `ninja: build stopped: interrupted by user.` and `exit=130`,
which looks like a human Ctrl-C but is the harness. Seen 2026-09-14 on a
725-step JusPrin rebuild.

**Why:** the notification says "completed" and the log shows no compiler
error, so it is easy to misread as a finished build; the changed files had not
compiled at all.

**How to apply:** for anything longer than a few minutes, start it detached
(`nohup sh -c "cmake --build … > log 2>&1; echo exit=\$? >> log" & disown`),
then arm a Monitor on the log that reports progress and the `exit=` line. Check
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' log` before trusting the result. Related:
[[track-wall-clock-on-background-work]], [[jusprin-worktree-build]].

The page sends every skill once per connection with the `skills` bridge message. A skill with a trigger is the app's: when the event it names happens, the host adds it to the one request where the model first reads about the event, as the request's last item, and to no later request. The first skill is `file-loaded` (trigger `file_loaded`): the first message after a file is opened or imported is a judgement about the load report.
